messages.subject: Basics of Shiny 0.4.0
parts:
Hi,

I have developed a simple app using the previous version of Shiny and it works fine.
A few days ago, I installed the newest version of Shiny and have tried to revise and run my app using it.
However, I have faced some problems with regard to the reactivity of the app.
When I first run the app, everything looks fine. I mean that the webpage displays the right outputs based on my defaults values. When I start changing my inputs, my main panel dose not get updated. I am aware of the changes in Shiny 0.4.0. However I am not able to resolve the problem.

For the sake of this post I have changed, renamed and shortened my app's elements.
What I am going to do using this app is to subset a master dataset and present some of the subset's characteristics.
So, I have an R function ("Fun_main") which takes care of subsetting using 5 inputs (MedicationName, CityName, StartDay, EndDay, and Dose). Any change to any of these 5 inputs should result in a different subset. Accordingly, the outputs "summary", "histogram", and "head" records change.

I have included below my server and ui codes revised based on my understanding from the Shiny 0.4.0.
Would you please help me find out why my app's reactivity feature does not work? In other words, my changes to the inputs do not change the outputs.

Thank you.

####Shiny UI####
library(shiny)

shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(
  
  headerPanel("My Test Application"),  
  sidebarPanel(    
    selectInput("MedicationName", "Choose a medication:", choices = c("aspirin", "amoxicillin", "acetaminophen", "cefazolin")),    
    selectInput("CityName", "Choose a city", choices = c("miami", "buffalo")),    
    selectInput("StartDay", "Start Day: ", choices = c("1", "2", "3")),
    selectInput("EndDay", "End Day: ", choices = c("15", "25", "35")),
    selectInput("Dose", "Dose: ", choices = c("10", "20", "30"))    
  ),
  
  mainPanel(     
    
    verbatimTextOutput("summary"),     
    tableOutput("view"),    
    plotOutput("main_plot")     
  )
))

####Shiny Server####
library(shiny)

shinyServer(function(input, output) {
  
  source("Fun_main.R") #This is my R function which does subsetting
  
  MedicationNameInput <- reactive({
    switch(input$MedicationName,
           "aspirin" = aspirin,
           "amoxicillin" = amoxicillin,
           "acetaminophen" = acetaminophen,
           "cefazolin" = cefazolin)           
  })
  
  CityNameInput <- reactive({
    switch(input$CityName,
           "miami" = miami,
           "buffalo" = buffalo)
  })
  
  StartDayInput <- reactive({
    switch(input$StartDay,
           "1" = 1,
           "2" = 2, 
           "3" = 3)
  })
  
  EndDayInput <- reactive({
    switch(input$EndDay,
           "15" = 15,
           "25" = 25, 
           "35" = 35)
  })
  
  DoseInput <- reactive({
    switch(input$Dose,
           "10" = 10,
           "20" = 20, 
           "30" = 30)
  })
  
  
  subsetDataset <- reactive({
    
    Fun_main(input$MedicationName, input$CityName, input$StartDay, input$EndDay, input$Dose)
    
  })
  
  output$summary <- renderPrint({
    
    subset <- subsetDataset() 
    summary(subset)
  })
  
  output$view <- renderTable({
    
    subset <- subsetDataset()
    head(subset, n=5)    
  })
  
  output$main_plot <- renderPlot({
    subset <- subsetDataset()
    Age <- unique(subset$AGE))
    hist(Age, probability = FALSE, breaks = 10, xlab = "Age Range (year)", main = "Subset's Age Distribution")
  })  
})

Hi Joe,

Thank you for confirming that my codes were correct. It helped me focus on my Fun_main and its nested functions. 
 Just for the records, the main issue was with the Fun_main. In the testing process, I added some constant inputs to the Fun_main which I forgot to remove them so it caused all the issues that I was reporting.

I also had to modify one line of my Shiny server code as follows:

Fun_main(input$MedicationName, input$CityName, as.numeric(input$StartDay), as.numeric(input$EndDay), as.numeric(input$Dose))

Again thank you.
